standard.title: Criteria for Design and Construction of Precast Concrete Trusses and Purlins (First Revision)
standard.sector: Civil Engineering / Planning, Housing and Prefabricated Construction

sectional_committee.name: Planning, Housing and Prefabricated Construction Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard provides the structural design, manufacturing, handling, assembly, and erection criteria for precast reinforced and prestressed concrete trusses and purlins primarily used in industrial and warehouse roofing.
standard.scope: This standard provides the structural design, manufacturing, handling, assembly, and erection criteria for precast reinforced and prestressed concrete trusses and purlins primarily used in industrial and warehouse roofing.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Compliance is strictly required under Public Works Department (PWD) specifications and industrial building tenders across India.
requirements: Structural analysis must explicitly account for additional dynamic loads and reversals of stresses occurring during demoulding, transport, lifting, and final positioning, which often govern design.
Recommended spacing for precast trusses is typically 6.0 m. Bowstring trusses utilizing curved top chords are preferred for material optimization and cost efficiency.
To prevent handling cracks and withstand shear forces, a minimum transverse reinforcement of 4 mm diameter steel bars must be detailed in all precast elements.
Precast purlins are typically spaced between 1.35 m and 1.40 m. Purlins must be analyzed for biaxial bending under gravity and wind loads acting perpendicular to sloping roof surfaces.
The locations of lifting inserts or loops must be mathematically calculated, clearly detailed in shop drawings, and marked on the physical cast elements to prevent structural failure during erection.
